superpowers.note: Verified claims (m at viewer.rs:1647, help-toggle ordering, no Line Default needed) hold; line+text anchor survives offline edits, never overwrites corrupt store, and the failure table and guards are explicit.

code-design.note: Excellent signatures and numbered call chains, but stores a bare source line so edits between sessions or on reload silently misplace marks, and the new ViewMode::MarkPending variant would trip render_frame's suppress_images check (viewer.rs:2438) unnoticed.

plain.note: Accurate current-state claims and text-fingerprint anchors, but a corrupt marks file is treated as empty and then overwritten, pruning on every write, and the function-level detail is thinner.

feature-dev.note: Accurate file:line citations and the most features (reload remap, margin letter, '' jump-back, NavEntry), but bare-line storage cannot repair offline edits and it grows scope with four modules and 15 commits.

reason: W combined a content-fingerprint anchor (robust to edits between sessions, the core need for persistent marks) with explicit failure behavior for corrupt, unwritable and concurrent stores, and nested-list stamping refinements, while staying small. Z was thorough and well-verified but stores only line numbers and over-expands scope; X had the best call-chain clarity but a weaker anchor model and a missed ViewMode side effect.
